headline: HSC exams likely to continue under all boards except Chattogram
summary: Education ministry officials decide to proceed with exams despite student protests in Dhaka over flooding and question errors.
details: Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are likely to continue as scheduled for all education boards except Chattogram, according to education ministry officials.
The decision was reached during a virtual meeting chaired by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon to review the national situation.
The announcement follows protests by HSC examinees in Dhaka, who demanded the postponement of remaining exams and the resignation of the education minister.
Protesters and guardians blocked the Science Laboratory intersection, citing heavy rain, flooding, and waterlogging that forced some candidates to travel by boat to reach centers.
Students also alleged administrative shortcomings and errors in the question papers of the examinations.
The unrest escalated as protesters marched toward Dhaka University, leading to a brief confrontation with police near VC Chattar.
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel were subsequently deployed in the Dhaka University area to maintain order.
caption:
HSC exams to proceed despite student protests and flooding. Only Chattogram board is the exception.

Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are likely to continue as scheduled for all education boards except Chattogram, according to education ministry officials.

The decision was reached during a virtual meeting chaired by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon to review the national situation.

The announcement follows protests by HSC examinees in Dhaka, who demanded the postponement of remaining exams and the resignation of the education minister.

Protesters and guardians blocked the Science Laboratory intersection, citing heavy rain, flooding, and waterlogging that forced some candidates to travel by boat to reach centers.

Students also alleged administrative shortcomings and errors in the question papers of the examinations.

The unrest escalated as protesters marched toward Dhaka University, leading to a brief confrontation with police near VC Chattar.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel were subsequently deployed in the Dhaka University area to maintain order.

headline_marked: Tarique Rahman: [[Keep ‘hybrids’ out of BNP]] to protect party unity
headline: Tarique Rahman: Keep ‘hybrids’ out of BNP to protect party unity
summary: The BNP Chairman urged leaders and activists to remain alert against infiltrators and stressed that unity and discipline are crucial ahead of local government elections.
details: Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman addressed a meeting of local BNP leaders and activists at Barishal Shilpakala Academy on Monday.
He emphasized that no “hybrids” or infiltrators should be allowed into the party under any circumstances to maintain organizational strength.
Tarique Rahman stated that the BNP would participate in local government elections after completing its organizational preparations, with the timing to be decided after the monsoon.
He urged local leaders to select candidates for chairman and member posts through mutual discussions and to recognize the sacrifices of those who faced repression for over a decade.
The BNP Chairman warned that conspiracies from groups at home and abroad are still active and that unity is the necessary counter to such attempts.
He also instructed party members to ensure that upcoming Hindu community religious festivals are held peacefully, stressing that no unpleasant incidents should be allowed.

Regarding governance, he urged party leaders to make realistic commitments to the public rather than unfulfillable promises, noting that sustainable development requires more than just building flyovers.
He alleged that 17 years of mismanagement and corruption have pushed almost every sector toward destruction, including the destruction of state institutions.
caption:
No 'hybrids' or infiltrators in the party. Tarique Rahman calls for absolute unity as BNP prepares for local polls.

Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman addressed a meeting of local BNP leaders and activists at Barishal Shilpakala Academy on Monday.

He emphasized that no “hybrids” or infiltrators should be allowed into the party under any circumstances to maintain organizational strength.

Tarique Rahman stated that the BNP would participate in local government elections after completing its organizational preparations, with the timing to be decided after the monsoon.

He urged local leaders to select candidates for chairman and member posts through mutual discussions and to recognize the sacrifices of those who faced repression for over a decade.

The BNP Chairman warned that conspiracies from groups at home and abroad are still active and that unity is the necessary counter to such attempts.

He also instructed party members to ensure that upcoming Hindu community religious festivals are held peacefully, stressing that no unpleasant incidents should be allowed.

Regarding governance, he urged party leaders to make realistic commitments to the public rather than unfulfillable promises, noting that sustainable development requires more than just building flyovers.

He alleged that 17 years of mismanagement and corruption have pushed almost every sector toward destruction, including the destruction of state institutions.
